title: Chapter 3 Full Practice: Matrices, Determinant and Systems of Linear Equations

questions.text: What is the size of the matrix A =  egin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \ 4 & 5 & 6 \end{bmatrix}?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Matrix A of size m × n has m rows and n columns.' The given matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns, so its size is 2 × 3.

questions.text: What is the entry a₂₃ of the matrix A =  egin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \ 4 & 5 & 6 \ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'a_{ij} appears at the intersection of the i-th row and the j-th column.' a₂₃ is the entry in the 2nd row and 3rd column, which is 6.

questions.text: When are two matrices A and B considered equal?
options: A) When they have the same number of rows.
B) When they have the same number of columns.
C) When they have the same size and a_{ij} = b_{ij} for all i and j.
D) When they have the same determinant.
questions.correct_answer: C) When they have the same size and a_{ij} = b_{ij} for all i and j.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Two matrices of the same size, A = [a_{ij}] and B = [b_{ij}], are said to be equal if and only if a_{ij} = b_{ij}, for all i, j.'

questions.text: What is the sum of A =  egin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} and B =  egin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \ 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix}?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A + B = [a_{ij} + b_{ij}].' Adding corresponding entries: 1+5=6, 2+6=8, 3+7=10, 4+8=12.

questions.text: What is the result of scalar multiplication 3A for A =  egin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Scalar multiplication: αA = [α a_{ij}].' Multiplying every entry of A by 3 gives [[3, 6], [9, 12]].

questions.text: If A and B are matrices of the same size, which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Commutative Law: A + B = B + A.' Matrix addition is commutative.

questions.text: What is the additive identity matrix for a 2 × 2 matrix?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Identity Law: A + 0 = A.' The zero matrix is the additive identity.

questions.text: Solve for X in the matrix equation 2X + A = B, where A =  egin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \ -2 & 2 \end{bmatrix} and B =  egin{bmatrix} 6 & -4 \ 8 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
questions.explanation: The module states: '2X = B - A implies X = (1/2)(B - A).' B - A = [[2, -4], [10, -2]]. Multiplying by 1/2 gives X = [[1, -2], [5, -1]].

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a law of matrix addition?
questions.explanation: The module states the laws of matrix addition: Commutative, Associative, Identity, and Inverse. Matrix multiplication is NOT commutative, which is discussed later.

questions.text: If matrix A is multiplied by a scalar α, what is the size of the resulting matrix?
options: A) It becomes a 1 × n matrix.
B) It becomes an m × 1 matrix.
C) It remains the same size m × n.
D) It becomes an n × m matrix.
questions.correct_answer: C) It remains the same size m × n.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Closure Law of Scalar Multiplication: αA is an m × n matrix.' Scalar multiplication does not change the size of the matrix.

questions.text: What is the condition for the product AB of two matrices A and B to be defined?
options: A) The number of rows in A must equal the number of columns in B.
B) The number of columns in A must equal the number of rows in B.
C) A and B must have the same size.
D) A and B must be square matrices.
questions.correct_answer: B) The number of columns in A must equal the number of rows in B.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The product AB of two matrices A and B is defined only if the number of columns in A and the number of rows in B are equal.'

questions.text: If A is a 2 × 3 matrix and B is a 3 × 4 matrix, what is the size of the product AB?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If A = [a_{ij}]_{m × n} and B = [b_{ij}]_{n × p}, then AB is an m × p matrix.' For A (2×3) and B (3×4), AB is 2 × 4.

questions.text: Compute the product AB for A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]].
What is the product BA for A = [[0, 1], [0, 0]] and B = [[1, 0], [0, 0]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'BA = [[0, 1], [0, 0]].' This example shows that matrix multiplication is not commutative.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about matrix multiplication in general?
options: A) AB = BA for all matrices A and B.
C) AB is always a scalar.
D) AB is always a zero matrix.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Matrix multiplication is not commutative. For matrices A and B given above, we have AB ≠ BA.'

questions.text: For which type of matrices is it always true that AB = BA?
options: B) Diagonal matrices of the same size
questions.correct_answer: B) Diagonal matrices of the same size
questions.explanation: The module states: 'More generally, if A and B are any two diagonal matrices of the same size, then AB = BA.'

questions.text: What is the product of the diagonal matrices A = [[2, 0], [0, 3]] and B = [[4, 0], [0, 5]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'AB = [[8, 0], [0, 15]].' Diagonal matrices multiply by multiplying the corresponding diagonal entries.

questions.text: What is the associative property of matrix multiplication?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Matrix multiplication is associative, i.e., whenever the products are defined, we have A(BC) = (AB)C.'
The module verifies that A(BC) = (AB)C. BC = [[2, 1], [4, 0]], A(BC) = [[-1, 16], [2, 24]].

questions.text: If A is a 3×3 matrix, what is the size of A²?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'We shall write Aⁿ for the product AAA...A (n terms).' A² = A × A, which is 3×3 × 3×3 = 3×3.

questions.text: What is a square matrix?
options: A) A matrix with more rows than columns.
B) A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
C) A matrix with more columns than rows.
D) A matrix with all entries equal to zero.
questions.correct_answer: B) A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A matrix A is said to be square if it has the same number of rows and columns.'

questions.text: What is an identity matrix?
options: A) A matrix with all entries equal to 1.
B) A square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.
C) A matrix with all entries equal to 0.
D) A matrix with 1s in the first row and 0s elsewhere.
questions.correct_answer: B) A square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A square matrix A is called an identity matrix if a_{ij} = 1 when i = j, and a_{ij} = 0 when i ≠ j.'

questions.text: What is a diagonal matrix?
options: A) A matrix where all entries are 1.
B) A matrix where all entries off the main diagonal are 0.
C) A matrix with all entries equal to 0.
D) A matrix with 1s in the first column.
questions.correct_answer: B) A matrix where all entries off the main diagonal are 0.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A square matrix D is said to be diagonal if d_{ij} = 0 whenever i ≠ j.'

questions.text: What is the transpose of matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Row 1 of matrix A becomes column 1 of Aᵗ, and row 2 of A becomes column 2 of Aᵗ.' Thus, Aᵗ = [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]].

questions.text: When is a square matrix A called symmetric?
options: C) When A is upper triangular.
D) When A is lower triangular.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A square matrix A is said to be Symmetric if A = Aᵗ.'

questions.text: Which of the following is a symmetric matrix?
questions.explanation: Matrix B is symmetric because Bᵗ = B. Matrix C is a diagonal matrix, which is always symmetric because Cᵗ = C. Matrix A is not symmetric because Aᵗ ≠ A.

questions.text: What is (Aᵗ)ᵗ equal to?
questions.explanation: The module states: '(Aᵗ)ᵗ = A.' The transpose of the transpose returns the original matrix.

questions.text: What is the transpose of the product (AB)ᵗ?
questions.explanation: The module states: '(AB)ᵗ = BᵗAᵗ.' The order of multiplication is reversed when taking the transpose of a product.

questions.text: What is a scalar matrix?
options: A) A diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal to 1.
B) A diagonal matrix in which all diagonal entries are equal.
C) Any matrix with all entries equal.
questions.correct_answer: B) A diagonal matrix in which all diagonal entries are equal.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A diagonal matrix in which all diagonal entries are equal is called a scalar matrix.'

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar matrix?
questions.explanation: A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix where all diagonal entries are equal. A is the identity matrix (scalar with 1s). B is a scalar matrix with 2s. C is a diagonal matrix but not scalar because 2 ≠ 3.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an elementary row operation?
options: A) Interchanging two rows: R_i ↔ R_j
B) Multiplying a row by a nonzero scalar: R_i → αR_i
C) Adding a multiple of one row to another: R_i → R_i + αR_j
D) Adding a column to another column
questions.correct_answer: D) Adding a column to another column
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The following are known as elementary row operations: 1. Interchanging two rows; 2. Multiplying a row by a nonzero scalar; 3. Adding a multiple of one row to another.' Column operations are not elementary row operations.

questions.text: In the row echelon form of a matrix, which of the following is NOT a required condition?
options: A) All nonzero rows are above any rows of all zeros.
B) Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.
C) All entries in a column below a leading entry are zeros.
questions.explanation: The module states the conditions for row echelon form. Condition 4 (leading entry is 1) is only required for reduced row echelon form, not for row echelon form.

questions.text: What additional conditions must a matrix in row echelon form satisfy to be in reduced row echelon form?
options: A) All nonzero rows are above zero rows.
B) The leading entry in each nonzero row is 1, and each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column.
C) All entries in a column below a leading entry are zeros.
D) The leading entries step to the right.
questions.correct_answer: B) The leading entry in each nonzero row is 1, and each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If a matrix in row echelon form satisfies: 4. The leading entry in each nonzero row is 1. 5. Each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column, then it is in reduced row echelon form.'

questions.text: What is the rank of a matrix A?
options: A) The number of rows in A.
B) The number of columns in A.
C) The number of nonzero rows in the reduced row echelon form of A.
D) The number of zero rows in the row echelon form of A.
questions.correct_answer: C) The number of nonzero rows in the reduced row echelon form of A.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Rank of an m × n matrix A, denoted by rank(A), is the number of nonzero rows of the reduced row echelon form of A.'

questions.text: What is the rank of matrix A = [[1, 1, 2], [2, 2, 5], [3, 3, 2]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'After a sequence of elementary row operations, we obtain the reduced echelon form of A, which has two nonzero rows. Thus, rank(A) = 2.'

questions.text: What is the relationship between the rank of a matrix A and the rank of its transpose Aᵗ?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The matrix A and its transpose Aᵗ have the same rank. That is, rank(A) = rank(Aᵗ).'

questions.text: Given the matrix A = [[4, 3], [2, 1]], which elementary row operation will produce the lower triangular matrix?
questions.explanation: The module asks: 'Use elementary row operations to find the lower triangular matrix which is row equivalent to A.' For A = [[4, 3], [2, 1]], R₂ → R₂ - (1/2)R₁ gives a zero below the diagonal.

questions.text: How many pivot positions does the matrix A = [[1, 1, 2], [2, 2, 5], [3, 3, 2]] have?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'A pivot position in a matrix A is a location in A that corresponds to a leading 1 in the reduced row echelon form of A.' Since rank(A) = 2, there are 2 pivot positions.

questions.text: Which of the following matrices is in reduced row echelon form?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Reduced row echelon form requires the leading entry in each nonzero row is 1, and each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column.' The identity matrix satisfies this.

questions.text: When using the algorithm to find the reduced row echelon form, what is the first step?
options: A) Begin with the leftmost nonzero column. This is a pivot column.
B) Create zeros above each pivot.
D) Replace rows to create zeros below the pivot.
questions.correct_answer: A) Begin with the leftmost nonzero column. This is a pivot column.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Step 1: Begin with the leftmost nonzero column. This is a pivot column. The pivot position is at the top.'

questions.text: What is the determinant of the matrix A = [[5, 2], [3, 4]]?
What is the minor M₁₂(A) for the matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'M₁₂(A) is the determinant of the submatrix obtained by deleting the 1st row and 2nd column.' Deleting row 1 and column 2 leaves [[4, 6], [7, 9]].

questions.text: What is the cofactor C₁₂(A) for the matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'C₁₂(A) = (-1)^(1+2) M₁₂(A) = -M₁₂(A).' The sign for position (1,2) is negative.

questions.text: Compute the determinant of A = [[2, 4, 0], [3, -1, 2], [2, 1, 1]].
Which of the following is a property of determinants?
options: C) If two rows are equal, det(A) = 0.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'det(A) = det(Aᵗ)' (Theorem 3.8), 'det(AB) = det(A)det(B)' (Theorem 3.10), and 'If two rows (or columns) are equal, then det(A) = 0.' All are correct.

questions.text: If B is obtained from A by interchanging two rows, what is the relationship between det(B) and det(A)?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If matrix B is obtained from matrix A by interchanging any two rows (R_i ↔ R_j), then det(B) = -det(A).'

questions.text: If B is obtained from A by multiplying a row by a nonzero scalar α, what is the relationship between det(B) and det(A)?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If matrix B is obtained from matrix A by multiplying the i-th row by a nonzero scalar α, then det(B) = α det(A).'

questions.text: What happens to the determinant when you add a multiple of one row to another row?
options: A) The determinant is multiplied by the scalar.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If matrix B is obtained from matrix A by adding a scalar multiple of one row to the other (R_i → R_i + α R_j), then det(B) = det(A).'

questions.text: What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix with diagonal entries 2, 3, and 5?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of the entries in the main diagonal.' 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.

questions.text: If det(A) = 2 and det(B) = 3, what is det(AB)?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'det(AB) = det(A)det(B).' 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.text: What is the adjoint of a matrix A?
options: A) The matrix of cofactors of A.
B) The transpose of the matrix of cofactors of A.
questions.correct_answer: B) The transpose of the matrix of cofactors of A.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Adj(A) = [C_{ij}(A)]^t. That is, adjoint of matrix A is the transpose of the matrix of cofactors for A.'

questions.text: What is the inverse of A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] using the adjoint formula?
What is the condition for a matrix A to be invertible?
options: C) A is a square matrix.
D) A is a diagonal matrix.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If A is invertible (nonsingular) then det(A) ≠ 0.'

questions.text: In Gauss-Jordan elimination, what is the initial augmented matrix used to find A⁻¹?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Write the n × 2n matrix that consists of A on the left and the n × n identity matrix I_n on the right to obtain [A | I_n].'

questions.text: What is the inverse of the diagonal matrix A = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 2, 0], [0, 0, 3]]?
questions.explanation: The module shows the Gauss-Jordan elimination for this matrix and concludes: 'A⁻¹ = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1/2, 0], [0, 0, 1/3]].'

questions.text: What is (AB)⁻¹ equal to?
questions.explanation: The module states: '(AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.' The order of multiplication is reversed for the inverse of a product.

questions.text: What is (Aᵗ)⁻¹ equal to?
questions.explanation: The module states: '(Aᵗ)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)ᵗ.' The inverse of the transpose is the transpose of the inverse.

questions.text: What is (αA)⁻¹ equal to?
questions.explanation: The module states: '(αA)⁻¹ = (1/α)A⁻¹.'

questions.text: If A is a 2×2 matrix with det(A) = 4, what is det(A⁻¹)?
questions.explanation: Since A⁻¹ = (1/det(A))Adj(A) and det(Adj(A)) = det(A)^(n-1), det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A) = 1/4 for a 2×2 matrix.

questions.text: If A is invertible and AB = AC, what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Suppose A is invertible. If AB = AC or BA = CA, then B = C.'

questions.text: What is the augmented matrix for the system 0.3l + 0.2h = 550, 0.2l + 0.4h = 500, 0.4l + 0.3h = 750?
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix is formed by appending the column vector b to the coefficient matrix A. For this system, [A|b] = [[0.3, 0.2 | 550], [0.2, 0.4 | 500], [0.4, 0.3 | 750]].

questions.text: What are the three possible outcomes for a system of linear equations?
options: A) One solution, two solutions, or three solutions.
B) Unique solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution.
C) Only one solution or no solution.
D) Only infinitely many solutions or no solution.
questions.correct_answer: B) Unique solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'For a system of linear equations, precisely one of the following is true: 1. It admits a unique solution; 2. It has infinitely many solutions; 3. It has no solution.'

questions.text: What is the first step in Gaussian elimination?
options: A) Find the inverse of the coefficient matrix.
B) Write the augmented matrix for the linear system.
D) Compute the determinant of the coefficient matrix.
questions.correct_answer: B) Write the augmented matrix for the linear system.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Gaussian Elimination: (a) Write the augmented matrix for the linear system.'

questions.text: What is the rank condition for a system to have a unique solution?
options: A) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) < number of unknowns.
B) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = number of unknowns.
questions.correct_answer: B) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = number of unknowns.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = number of unknowns, then the linear system has only one solution.'

questions.text: Using Cramer's rule, what is x₁ for the system x₁ + x₂ = 1, x₁ - x₂ = 3?
What is the solution to the system x₁ + x₂ = 1, x₁ - x₂ = 3 using the inverse method?
When does Cramer's rule fail to solve a linear system?
options: A) When the system has infinitely many solutions.
B) When the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero.
C) When the system is inconsistent.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Cramer's rule doesn't work if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero or the coefficient matrix is not square.' If det(A) = 0, the system may have no solution or infinitely many solutions.

questions.text: What is the solution set for the system x₁ + 2x₂ + x₃ = 2, x₁ - x₂ - 2x₃ = -1?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The system has infinitely many solutions, and the set of solutions is given by {(1 - α, α, 1 - α) : α ∈ ℝ}.'

questions.text: What is the rank condition for a system to have infinitely many solutions?
options: A) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) = number of unknowns.
B) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) < number of unknowns.
questions.correct_answer: B) rank(A) = rank([A|b]) < number of unknowns.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'If rank(A) = rank([A|b]) < number of unknowns, then the linear system has infinitely many solutions.'

questions.text: Using the inverse method, what is the solution to 4x₁ - 2x₂ + 3x₃ = 0, 2x₁ + 2x₂ + 5x₃ = 0, 8x₁ - 5x₂ - 2x₃ = 0?
questions.explanation: This is a homogeneous system (b = 0). Since the coefficient matrix is invertible (det ≠ 0), the only solution is the trivial solution x = (0, 0, 0).
